title: [YouPass Collect] - High school education levels across six countries in 2010

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the percentages of adults who had completed high school education across two age brackets in six different nations in 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, younger adults aged 25-34 generally had higher high school completion rates than their older counterparts aged 55-64 in most countries surveyed, with the notable exception of the USA. Additionally, South Korea recorded the highest proportion among younger adults, while China registered the lowest figures for both age groups.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding nations with high educational attainment, Germany showed relatively similar rates between the two cohorts, with 83.5% of older adults and 88% of younger adults having finished high school. In contrast, the USA was the only country where the older generation slightly surpassed the younger one, with 91% and 88%, respectively. Meanwhile, Russia exhibited a more pronounced gap, as the figure for 25-34 year-olds stood at 92%, significantly higher than that of the 55-64 age bracket, at 70%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining countries, South Korea demonstrated the most dramatic generational difference, with high school completion soaring from 43% among older adults to 98.5% among younger ones. Brazil showed moderate rates, with 25% and 52% for the older and younger groups, in that order. Finally, China recorded the lowest educational attainment across both demographics, at 11% and 20%, respectively.
